You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Adobe Q3 Earnings Preview: Can 90 Million Free Users Convert Into Paid Growth?

TEXT:
1. Investment Snapshot
Adobe (ADBE.US) reports fiscal Q3 2026 results after the U.S. close on September 10, 2026 . Street consensus is roughly $6.69 billion in revenue (about +11.7% YoY) and $6.08 in non-GAAP EPS (about +14.5% YoY). Company guidance is revenue of $6.67–$6.72 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $6.05–$6.10 .
The stock has been under pressure for the past year and is down about 18% year to date. The debate is not current-quarter profitability. It is whether free users and AI features can convert into durable ARR . This print is a test of the “land users first, monetize later” model.
2. Four Things That Matter
Focus 1: Can 90 million free users enter the paid funnel?
Adobe is shifting from “ charge for pro tools” to “user scale + AI usage.” Creative freemium MAU rose from more than 50 million to more than 90 million in Q2 (over +70% YoY). Adobe.com traffic was up more than 50% YoY. Acrobat + Express MAU topped 850 million (about +20% YoY).
The market is not scoring MAU expansion alone. It wants conversion and usage intensity. If creation stays on ChatGPT, Claude and similar platforms and never returns to Adobe for professional editing and brand control, the old software moat keeps shrinking.
Focus 2: Is AI moving from product launch to measurable revenue?
Q2 AI-first ARR topped $500 million (more than 3x YoY). Firefly ARR rose about +50% QoQ and exited near $300 million . Getting AI in front of users is largely done. The harder step is proving usage creates incremental revenue rather than just higher acquisition cost. Commentary on Firefly, Creative Agent and GenStudio will shape how the Street prices FY27 paid growth.
Focus 3: ARR quality versus the 10.2% full-year target
Q2 ending ARR was $27.1 billion (+12.5% YoY), including about $480 million from the Semrush close. The full-year ARR growth target remains 10.2% . The Street worries organic growth is being diluted by freemium expansion and deferred price actions.
If Q3 net new ARR improves and AI-first / Firefly stay strong, earnings quality gets support. If free users keep growing while ARR does not, the model gets re-rated lower.
Focus 4: CEO transition and distribution shift
Anil Chakravarthy takes over on December 1 from Shantanu Narayen after 18 years. An internal handoff implies continuity, not a reset. Creative Agent is already inside Photoshop, Premiere and other core apps, and the Topaz Labs deal is meant to strengthen on-device models. The Saudi partnership covers more than 27 million eligible users and is valued at more than $4 billion . Near-term revenue is limited. What matters is whether these move s enter enterprise budgets, raise usage frequency and re-accelerate ARR.
3. Upside and Downside
Upside catalysts:
Net new ARR beats, supporting the 10.2% full-year target.
AI-first and Firefly stay hot , with better free-to-paid conversion.
Management gives a clearer FY27 monetization path.
Downside risks:
Results only hit the midpoint of guidance, with no ARR improvement.
Free users keep growing while conversion stays weak.
Generative AI siphons pro workflows, and guidance turns conservative during the CEO transition.
4. Trading Notes
Tactical notes (ADBE, as of September 8 close $257.26 ):
Into the print: Price rejected 294–295 , lost the 20-day (about 273 ), then broke the 200-day (about 267.6 ). It is now testing the 50-day (about 250 ). Risk/reward into the event is only average. Implied move is about 8% , IV is elevated. Keep event risk light. Avoid adding leveraged longs below 250 .
Long setup: A close back above 268–276 , with pullbacks holding 250–254 . Upside references 285–295 , then 306 / 330 . Stops can sit at 248 , or below 240 / 220 depending on risk tolerance.
Short / hedge setup: A gap that cannot reclaim 250–254 , or a failed push through 268–276 . Downside references 244 / 240 / 220 , with 190 as the extreme (near the 52-week low).
Key numbers: Total revenue and non-GAAP EPS versus guidance; total ARR / net new ARR and the 10.2% full-year target; AI-first ARR, Firefly ARR and paid conversion.
If results and guidance are both strong, look for pullbacks after the initial squeeze. If the print is only in-line and ARR quality is weak, watch the after-hours gap and IV crush. Size and stops should match personal risk tolerance. Do not chase a one-way move at a high-volatility event.
